Full Review after two nights of tests :

I picked up the Scout pack so I could test all four products.

UVO Necklace : A small disk on a lanyard that was the most packed with crystals. Gave it six seconds of charge from a 500lm torch. Despite being the smallest piece, it provided more concentrated light than the bigger pieces. A little awkward to use as a reading light due to it's shape and lanyard. Charge lasted for about 5 hours. I mainly see it used as attached to my ruck or smaller kit backs to find in the dark, or attached to the ruck for visibility for someone walking behind me to follow. Maybe worn around the neck and pulled out for map navigation at night. Pleased with the product.

UV Paqlite Small : A sealed plastic bag with the crystals spread throughout. Crystals not tightly packed together, so offers much more diffused light. Same as before, about 6 seconds charge and it was fairly effective for about 6 hours. My problem with this piece is that it is advertised as "hangs up inside a dark environment, like a 2-3 person tent, to provide a night light illumination all night long." and a small metal chain will allow you to hang it. The emphasis is on "dark environment" ... and "small space" ... as the light is diffused, it is very low level light. You eyes if not adjusted to night vision, will see very little unless the light is very close to an object. If your eyes have been given the time to adjust before using the paqlite, it does actually illuminate a small space and seems bright. If your eyes are not adjusted, then it seems as if it does not light up any space adequately. Easy to read with and used it as a bookmark before I slept. Even though much bigger than the necklace, it would perform all the same tasks in addition to being slightly better at lighting up a confined space.

UVGlostik : About 4inches. A small rounded bar with a flat bottom. Again, comes with a small lanyard to enable attaching. The second most packed with crystals and the second brightest of the four. Effective for lighting up a very small space (hammock interior) or 1 person tent with the caveat that once again, only really works once your eyes have adjusted to night vision. Effective like the others for marking and attaching. The flat bottom makes it the most effective for maps or reading as you slide it along the paper. I like it.

Tooblite : The one that actually looks like a glowstick but doesn't perform as a glowstick if you are expecting similar results. The crystals were very erratic. Small areas of highly condensed and large areas with very few. The bottom third of the stick is almost clear, and as a result, there is no light from there. This one made me think that it is completely random as to how many crystals you receive in a product and as the crystals determine the light level, every product is a crap shoot. It's the biggest of the pieces and doesn't do anything the other three do better. It's not a glowstick, seemed to lose its charge quicker, about 4 hours, maybe closer to 3. It was the dimmest, but again, it may have something to do with having few crystals. As a marker, it would do the job, but I'd rather use the other three for any other task. Maybe I was just unlucky, but I don't recommend it if you can buy the others, or if you want to take a chance on the amount of crystal you receive in it.
